docs.t: New: opening an .AppImage, .bin or .run file (Linux programs that need no installing) shows what it is, with Run and "Keep it in the Start menu". It runs in Linux (Debian) from where it is.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Linux programs in Debian can use the camera and game controllers (also Steam Input's virtual controllers), including ones plugged in after Linux started. Cameras now belong to the desktop user's own group, which Debian's user shares.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: New (test): System Settings › Desktop engine: Standard (Chromium) or Lite (WebKit). Lite runs the desktop and its apps in WebKit, a lighter web engine that took about a third of Chromium's memory in a trial, and opens websites in Chromium's own window. The change applies when the computer restarts; if Lite does not start, Standard takes over for that start. Lite's engine (WebKitGTK) is part of Rudolf OS itself, so it works with or without Linux (Debian) and with "Encrypt my data"; videos in H.264 or AAC play only with Standard for now.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: a USB stick made in Settings › Storage and backup is a rescue stick for this computer. Recovery mode on it starts this computer's own Rudolf OS with safe settings (and the stick's own when this computer has none that can start); a normal start runs the stick's own Rudolf OS. The stick gets the boot files of the system it copies, downloaded when the drive's own are older (on a test laptop, a stick with older boot files could not start Recovery mode at all). Each release now carries its boot files (boot.iso) for this. Help › Starting from a USB stick explains it, with the boot-menu keys and Fast Boot.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Force quit, on an app's right-click menu below Close (a window's title bar and taskbar button, a Linux or Windows program's taskbar button, the Start menu for a Linux app that runs) and in Task Manager's Apps: it ends the app with all its background processes at once, without asking it to quit, for apps that leave something running after they are closed (Steam's helpers, a tray app). For the desktop's own apps it closes all their windows at once.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: New: Task Manager's Processes has End process tree (as in Windows XP's Task Manager): it ends a process and every process it started, and theirs, such as all of Steam's helper processes at once. Processes Rudolf OS needs are left running. End process, End process tree and End now are also on a process's right-click menu.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: a selected or highlighted item in desktop windows (Settings' pages, File Explorer's files and folders, Task Manager's processes, the network list, menus and others) looks as in the Start menu: the accent colour with white writing, or black writing on a light accent colour. Before, some lists drew a light bar under the dark theme's light writing, and the text could not be read. Hovering over an item tints it with the accent colour and keeps the writing as it was.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: coming back to a computer whose screen had locked could show the lock screen twice (on an HP desktop), and the screen saver or the lock could start again just after waking or unlocking. Each idle check now waits at most 4 seconds for the system, one runs at a time, and one that saw you come back while it waited does nothing; waking from sleep counts as you being back; nothing locks by itself for a minute after unlocking (Lock and Windows+L still do). Updates and other background work also wait while the screen is locked, as they were meant to.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: on the Lite desktop the screen saver draws at most 15 frames a second at a lower resolution, leaving the processor to your apps.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: "Sign in with Google" on websites (claude.ai and others) stopped on a blank accounts.google.com window in the browser window (and could in Oracle's real tabs). Chromium's FedCM sign-in is turned off there, so Google uses its usual sign-in window, as in Firefox.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: with the Lite desktop, the notice when Oracle opens a website in the browser window says why (every website opens there with Lite), instead of speaking of signing in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: Task Manager is in the desktop's right-click menu, and Ctrl+Alt+Del opens it too (as Ctrl+Shift+Esc does), also from a game or an app in front: the desktop comes forward with it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: Task Manager opened with Ctrl+Alt+Del or Ctrl+Shift+Esc comes up above every window and stays there (Always on top), and while it is open the desktop's processes get the processor and the disk first, so a program that is using up the computer can still be found and ended. Closing it puts everything back. Opened from the menus it is an ordinary window.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: a window opened later no longer comes up over the windows set to Always on top.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: with the Lite desktop engine, dropdown menus (for example in System Settings) looked blank in the dark theme: WebKit drew them white with light text. They now look as they do with Standard.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: with the Lite desktop engine, a website opened from Oracle could open its browser window behind the desktop, so nothing seemed to happen; Oracle's "Show it again" brought it up.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: with the Lite desktop engine, the desktop restarted every few seconds with "Real browser tabs are ready": it offered Chromium's one-time restart into real tabs, which Lite does not use. Lite no longer offers it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: the Lite desktop engine (WebKit) closed as it started on real computers: a graphics library it loads while running (OpenGL ES, libGLESv2) was missing from Rudolf OS. The self-test now checks for it, and the release check runs Lite from the system itself, so a missing library is caught before a release.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: a desktop engine that cannot start no longer leaves the computer stuck. Lite (WebKit) that closes 3 times in a row as it starts, or that has not reached the sign-in screen when the computer is switched off, is turned off for good: Standard is used from the next moment on, and System Settings › Desktop engine says when and why. Choosing Lite again tries it once more. (On a test laptop, Lite closed as it started every few seconds and the computer never reached the sign-in screen.) The same goes for Oracle's real tabs (the shell): if it keeps closing, or the desktop asks for it again and again, the desktop page is used by itself until the next start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: a system update that cannot start because part of it is missing now goes back to the previous system by itself, instead of stopping at "this drive has boot files only".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Changed: Recovery mode starts this computer's installed system with safe settings (the standard desktop engine, no shell, safe graphics) and changes nothing. Before, it started the drive's own system, which most installed computers do not have ("this drive has boot files only"), or a USB stick's older system with this computer's newer files. Recovery mode works this way with boot files from 1.5.7 on (Settings › Update and recovery › boot files).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: a Rudolf OS started in Recovery mode, or running from a USB stick or a disc on a computer where Rudolf OS is installed, no longer updates the installed system (Settings says why). On a test laptop, a rescue stick put an update in place that needed the stick, and the laptop could not start without it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Fixed: an update never counts on a USB stick or disc staying plugged in: a part it shares with one is copied onto the computer's own drive, and an update is only made ready to start once every part of it is there.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Under the hood: a review of what rudolfd keeps in memory between requests (each request is a process of its own, so a value kept in one was lost in the next, as with Downloads in 1.5.6): every such value is now listed with why it is safe, and a test fails when a new one is added without that review.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.7 (in progress)
docs.t: Under the hood: Blitzen can read what this computer recorded (the health log, the service log, the desktop's errors, the last task's log), with lines that carry a password, token or key left out, and Rudolf OS's own documents (its plans, this list of changes and the Help pages), searched on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere; the diagnostics that use them come next.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Summary: your files on the disk (docs/plan-1.5.6.md)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Under the hood: Rudolf OS can keep each account's files as real files on the disk, encrypted with that account's own key and unreadable while it is signed out.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New (beta): accounts keep their files on the disk. Saving writes only the files that changed, large files have no size limit, and Linux apps see the same Documents, Pictures, Music and Videos.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New (beta): an account from before 1.5.6 moves its files to the disk once, in the background after signing in. Everything is read back and compared before the switch; a move that does not arrive whole changes nothing and is tried again at the next sign-in. The old copy is kept for 7 days, so going back to 1.5.5 still finds your files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New (beta): with your files on the disk, the Trash still gives back large files (they wait in your folder's own Trash until it is emptied), backups carry your home, a backup restored on another computer fills your folder there, and administrators can open, change and close other accounts' files as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: Power and battery is in Settings › System health, below the summary, instead of System Settings. The battery on the taskbar, User Settings' link and the Settings search go there.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: Battery care stops charging at 70 %, 80 %, 90 % or 100 % (it was 60 %, 80 % or 100 %). A limit of 60 % set before is kept as 70 %, the nearest choice, not raised to 100 %. If the battery reports a different limit than the one chosen (some batteries take only certain limits), Power and battery says so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: Bluetooth's page could fail when another Settings page was opened before it had loaded, and the encryption page when Rudolf OS gave no list of moved folders.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle's Downloads page still pointed at C:\DOWNLOADS, which 1.5.5 replaced with each account's own Downloads: "Open" gave 404 Not found and "Open Downloads folder" gave Folder not found. Both go to your Downloads now, and a file kept on the disk opened from Oracle opens the way File Explorer opens it. Small files Oracle downloads itself go straight into your Downloads.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: opening a Debian package (.deb, such as Discord's) says Rudolf OS does not install packages from a file yet, and offers the App Store, where most such apps (Discord among them) are.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: with your files on the disk, Linux apps' Downloads is your own Downloads, like Documents and Pictures. Nothing is copied back and forth any more. Copies the earlier 1.5.6 beta had made of your downloads in the Downloads folder shared by Linux apps are removed at sign-in (only exact copies), and files Linux apps saved there move into your Downloads when the computer has one account. Website downloads still arrive in a separate folder first, where they are checked. (Fixed in the second beta: with "Encrypt my data" on, that separate folder was not set up, because the encrypted folder is still locked at start-up, so website downloads could not be saved. Fixed again in the third beta: rudolfd forgot the separate folder after each request, so with your Downloads shared with Linux apps it looked for new downloads in the wrong place.)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: waking the computer from sleep restarted the browser (closing every window), because the desktop's "I'm alive" signal was as old as the sleep. The desktop now gets 90 seconds after waking to answer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: with your files on the disk, the old two-way copying between your Downloads and Linux apps' Downloads could still run when your Downloads could not be shared with Linux apps directly, and it deleted files it thought an app had deleted (on the Vivobook, DISCORD.DEB and an installer). It never runs for files on the disk now.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: a Linux app put on the desktop (Discord from the App Store, say) showed the penguin instead of its own icon. It now shows the app's icon, as the Start menu and the taskbar do. (An app installed from a Linux package, such as Discord's .deb, showed its icon at full size, over the other icons; it is icon-sized now.)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: no app could use the camera on an installed Rudolf OS (the Vivobook's built-in webcam, a USB webcam): the camera's device belonged to the system only. Cameras now belong to the video group the desktop is in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: programs in Linux (Debian), Wine among them, did not see your Documents, Pictures, Music, Videos and Downloads as they are since 1.5.6, and with "Encrypt my data" on they could not open Downloads at all. They now see the same folders as the rest of Rudolf OS, also after switching accounts.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed (third 1.5.6 beta): the installation wizard said a package in Downloads was "not a package in your folders": it gave the file's place in your account's folder, which Linux does not use. rudolfd now turns it into the name Linux sees.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: installing apps from files. Opening a Linux package (.deb, such as Discord's) shows what it is and installs it into Linux (Debian) with what it needs, with a progress bar; its app is then in the Start menu, and the wizard offers to open it or put it on the desktop. An iPhone or iPad app (.ipa) is explained: it cannot run outside Apple's devices. AppImages, .bin installers and Android apps follow.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: the Command Prompt and the Linux terminal are one app, Terminal, with the Command Prompt's icon. Each is a tab: ＋ opens either. Terminal opens on Linux when Linux is set up, otherwise on the Command Prompt (also in a web browser). Lua programs, .BAT files and rpk open a Command Prompt tab. Its desktop icon keeps its place.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: the Developer Console is out of the Start menu unless Settings › Apps › "Show developer tools in the Start menu" is on. It is always in Task Manager and in search.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: installing a Linux package also adds what it recommends once the package itself is in (Steam's package adds Valve's own source, whose 32-bit libraries can only be found then).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: Windows programs (.exe, .msi) open in the installation wizard: an installer runs with Wine and the programs it installs are offered (Open, Put on the desktop) as they appear; another program runs, or can be installed anyway. Without Wine (or Linux), the wizard sets them up first.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: the Install button on Flathub's website (in Oracle) gave "This site can't be reached". Its link, and a downloaded .flatpakref file, now open that app's page in the App Store.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: /dev/fd, /dev/stdin, /dev/stdout and /dev/stderr were missing. Steam (from the App Store) failed to start its interface because of it, and scripts using them failed too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: Alt+F4 with the desktop in front closed the desktop's whole window, back to the sign-in screen. It now closes the window in front, as everywhere else.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: when memory runs out and no web page can be closed, an app with no window open (Discord in the tray, say) is closed instead, never the app or game in front. System health says which.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: the compressed memory (zram) is as large as the computer's memory instead of half of it, so it can hold twice as much (on the Vivobook, Steam, Discord and a game filled the old one).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: while an app or game is in front and memory ran short, the desktop gets 5 minutes instead of 2 to answer before its browser is restarted (closing every window).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: the Weather widget said "Weather needs an internet connection" for 15 minutes after start-up when the desktop was ready before the Wi-Fi. It now tries again after 20 seconds, then 1, 2 and 5 minutes, and at once when the computer is online.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: a prompt that needs you (the development link's "Allow this command?", "Allow a remote connection?") waited behind a full-screen game or app where it could not be reached. It now comes to the front, and the app comes back once you answer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: an installer's window could stay hidden behind the desktop (Starport's installer in Wine: its wizard belongs to another window). A window's dialogs now stay above it with the keyboard, and a dialog whose owner is hidden is shown as a window of its own. The installation wizard has "Show the installer" and "Stop the installer".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: Chromium's own shortcuts could close, reload or cover the desktop: F5 and Ctrl+R reloaded it (every window lost), Ctrl+H, Ctrl+J, F1 and others put Chromium's pages over it, Shift+Esc opened Chromium's task manager. None of them acts on the desktop now; the desktop's own shortcuts still work. In Oracle's tabs Chromium's pages never open from a website, and Ctrl+Shift+R and Shift+F5 reload the tab.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: File Explorer sorts in every view (Sort by Name, Date modified, Type or Size, with the direction next to it), and remembers each folder's order for your account. Downloads opens newest first. View › "Folders first" can be switched off, and "Use this order for all folders" sets your default.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: favourite files. "Add to favourites" works for files too; they are listed in the sidebar below your favourite folders and open in their app. A favourite follows its file when you rename or move it in File Explorer, and stays greyed when the file is gone, with "Remove from favourites".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: Settings › Storage and backup says what fills the computer's disk, largest first: your files, other accounts' files, Downloads, the Trash, Linux apps, Steam's games, Linux (Debian), Emu's games, Blitzen's model, the system and everything else, each with what you can do about it (Open, Manage, Open Steam). "The disk is almost full" opens it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: the Trash shows its size (on the desktop and in its window, large files at their size on the disk), and Settings › Storage and backup can delete items for good once they are older than 1, 14, 30 or 60 days (Never by default; each account its own), with one notification a day at most.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: File Explorer's "Everywhere" search looks in the folder you are in first, then the rest of C:, then plugged-in drives (by name, at most 3 folder levels and 2,000 files each), with filters for the type (documents, pictures, music, videos, archives, programs) and when it changed. Results show where each one is and appear while it looks; it can be stopped, and shows 1,000 at a time with "Show more".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: Rename… with several files selected renames them together: a pattern ("HOLIDAY ###" gives HOLIDAY 001, 002…, each keeping its extension) or find and replace, with every new name shown first. Names that would clash are shown in red and nothing changes until they are fixed; one Undo puts all the names back.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: Find duplicates (a folder's menu in File Explorer, and Settings › Storage and backup) finds identical files (the same size and SHA-256, also for files kept on the disk), suggests keeping the newest of each, and moves the others to the Trash only when you ask.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: most accounts' files did not move to the disk on 1.5.6 ("Your files stay where they were" at every sign-in): account ids with capital letters were refused. Found by the new QEMU test of the move (t156).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: the move of an account's files to the disk stopped at its large downloads when the account's id had capital letters (their downloads folder is in lower case), and a move that did not finish left the account's folder unlocked after sign-out. Found by QEMU t156.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: when Linux (Debian) was started after signing in, the account's folders stayed in use after sign-out, so the names of its folders and files could still be listed (their contents could not be read). Found by QEMU t156.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: restoring a backup after the account's folder on the disk was removed did not bring the files back: the large files, which backups do not hold, stopped the move. They are now left out.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: closing Steam or Discord could leave the screen white for over a minute and then go back to the sign-in screen: the desktop's memory had been pushed into the compressed swap behind them. The desktop now keeps its memory (a memory group the system frees last), a reserve of free memory is kept for the graphics driver, and the watchdog waits up to 5 minutes while the desktop is still reading its memory back instead of restarting it after 1 minute. And closing a game no longer restarts the desktop the moment it comes back: behind a game it is not judged at all, and back in front it has a minute to answer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: the power button signed you out before asking what to do, so Cancel left you at the sign-in screen. It now asks first: Cancel goes back to the desktop as it was, Shut down and Restart sign out once chosen, and Sleep keeps you signed in behind the lock screen. The same for Start › Shut down.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: the Wi-Fi dropped every open connection whenever it moved between the router's 2.4 and 5 GHz radios. A short drop now keeps the network address (and renews it on the same network); the Wi-Fi looks for a better radio only when the signal is weak; Realtek rtw88 Wi-Fi chips (RTL8821CE and others) no longer use PCIe link power saving, a known cause of drops. When a change of radio fails and the Wi-Fi sets the network aside (on the Vivobook for 5.5 minutes), Rudolf OS takes it back within about 25 seconds. A radio of the router that does not answer is left out for the rest of the session (on the Vivobook the 2.4 GHz one, tried twice in 25 minutes, which disconnected a game), and allowed again if the Wi-Fi stays off the network for more than 10 seconds.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Fixed: Linux apps' icons (Discord, Steam) could stay a penguin for the whole session after one failed request; the icon is now asked for again. With Encrypt my data, Linux apps also went missing from the desktop and the Start menu after a restart (their list was asked for before sign-in opened the encrypted folder): the list is now kept and asked for again after sign-in, and their pictures drawn at once. The same for Debian's apps and Windows programs (Starport GE).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: Settings › Display Properties: 16 accent colours (8 before), and the accent colour on the taskbar and on the desktop icons, each with its own tick box and a choice of Normal, Negative or Complementary. The 16 colours stay on one row, a little smaller when the window needs it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: Settings › Display Properties › Taskbar › Style: Standard, Wireframe (outlines on a see-through bar), Monochrome (greys), Candy (glossy, round buttons) or Retro (raised and sunken edges on silver); each in the accent colour when that is ticked for the taskbar.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: Changed: the Start button and the "Rudolf OS 1.5.6" button beside it are one button: the logo with the name and the whole version, which opens the Start menu (Settings › About stays in Settings and the Start menu). On a taskbar at the left or the right the version is under the logo.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.6 (2026-11-10)
docs.t: New: every app in the Start menu has the same right-click menu: Open, Pin to taskbar, Add to (or Remove from) desktop and Properties, with Uninstall… for Linux apps from Flathub. Before, Linux apps and Windows programs had none and Emu only Open. Properties shows the app's details: what kind of app it is, its address (which File Explorer opens, to look at), its size on disk, the file types it uses, its program file, version, publisher, ID, and its pinned and desktop state.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Summary: each account has its own Downloads, choose the app shortcuts on your desktop, and the Trash's tooltip says what is in it

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Changed: each account has its own Downloads again (C:\USERS\<name>\DOWNLOADS), encrypted with its home folder; large downloads are kept on the disk in the account's own folder. From 1.2.7 to 1.5.4 every account shared C:\DOWNLOADS. At the first start of 1.5.5 that folder goes to its owner when the computer has one account; with several, it stays readable by all as C:\SHARED DOWNLOADS (BEFORE 1.5.5) for an administrator to sort out. Nothing is deleted.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Changed: a download that finishes while nobody is signed in waits, and goes to whoever signs in next. The guest's downloads are deleted when the guest signs out.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: app shortcuts can be taken off the desktop: right-click › Remove from desktop, the Delete key, dropping the icon on the Trash, or File Explorer's Desktop folder. The app stays in the Start menu.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: right-click an app in the Start menu › Add to desktop (or Remove from desktop). Apps without a desktop icon of their own get one. Before, Add to desktop only said "Already on the desktop".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Desktop icons… (in the desktop's right-click menu and in File Explorer's Desktop folder) lists every app with a tick for those on the desktop, and Restore the standard icons. Each account keeps its own choice.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: File Explorer › right-click › Copy to desktop.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Changed: My Computer and Programs cannot be dropped on the Trash (hide them from their menu instead). Desktop icons… lists the desktop's own icons by name, My Computer among them, and the notification after removing an icon puts it back with a click.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: the Trash's tooltip kept saying "The Trash is empty" after something was put in it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: the built-in microphones of AMD laptops (1.5.4) were found but not offered to apps: their sound card did not open with ALSA's use case files, so it is opened with the sound server's own settings instead (found on the ASUS Vivobook Go).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: after a restart, Downloads was only looked after once something was downloaded, so downloads from before 1.5.5 did not move into your own Downloads, and lost entries were not found again (found on the ASUS Vivobook Go).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: some downloads (for example Discord's and Steam's .deb files) stopped with "the site may offer it over an insecure connection": the browser was holding them for a confirmation it cannot ask for. It no longer does (Rudolf OS checks every file itself), and the message says what happened.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: Downloads no longer lists downloads as "Downloading…" for ever (from before a restart, or cancelled by the browser), and a saved file is no longer listed with another download's address.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.5 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: a download whose entry in Downloads was lost (for example one that finished while nobody was signed in) is listed again by itself, after the antivirus has checked it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Summary: Bluetooth on computers with an Intel, MediaTek, Qualcomm or Realtek chip, sound on laptops with an Intel sound processor or speaker amplifiers, the built-in microphones of AMD laptops, Windows games through Steam's Proton, and Thunderbolt and USB4 docks and displays

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Bluetooth works with Intel chips (the Bluetooth half of Intel Wi-Fi cards: 8260, 8265, 9260, 9560, AX200, AX201, AX203, AX210, AX211, AX411, BE200, BE201 and newer), MediaTek MT7921, MT7922 and MT7925, and Qualcomm chips on USB, as well as Realtek (1.5.1). Not yet tried on a computer with these chips: if Bluetooth does not appear, Settings › Devices › Not supported yet and Report a problem say what the computer has.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Bluetooth built into the board on a serial line (UART), found in inexpensive laptops and tablets (Realtek RTL8723BS and RTL8723CS, Broadcom, Intel, Qualcomm).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: the built-in microphones of AMD laptops whose microphones are wired to the AMD audio processor (ACP): Ryzen 4000 and 5000 (Renoir, Cezanne), 6000 and 7x20/7x30 (Rembrandt, Mendocino: the ASUS Vivobook Go among them), and 7040/8040 (Phoenix, Hawk Point), where the laptop is known to the kernel or its firmware says so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Changed: Settings › Sound offers only sound cards that play as outputs, and lists the microphones it found ("Built-in digital microphones (AMD audio processor)").

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: sound on laptops whose speakers and microphones go through Intel's sound processor (SOF): 11th to 13th generation Core (Tiger Lake, Alder Lake, Raptor Lake; Elkhart Lake) and Core Ultra (Meteor Lake, Arrow Lake, Lunar Lake, Panther Lake), including SoundWire laptops. Settings › Sound names it ("Intel sound processor (SOF)"). Not yet tried on such a laptop.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: the speaker amplifiers of many ASUS, Lenovo, HP and Dell laptops (Cirrus CS35L41, CS35L54 and CS35L56; TI TAS2563 and TAS2781), without which the speakers stay silent or very quiet while headphones work.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: a sound card that appears after start-up (Intel's sound processor once its firmware runs, a USB headset or speaker) is ready to use by itself, and one that is unplugged goes away from the list. Sound processors and USB sound cards are set up with ALSA's use case files, as on other systems; the HD Audio of most computers (the Vivobook's among them) is set up as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Windows games through Steam's Proton. Installing Steam from App Store › Games also installs the 32-bit graphics drivers Proton needs (a Steam installed earlier gets them the next time it is opened), and Rudolf OS gives games what Proton expects: NT synchronization (ntsync), more memory maps and more open files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Steam's card in App Store › Games says whether this computer's graphics have the Vulkan that Proton needs, and why not when they do not (drawing with the processor, Intel graphics before Broadwell, older NVIDIA cards, old Radeon cards, virtual machines); that games whose anti-cheat allows Linux work and others (Valorant, Fortnite, Call of Duty) do not, with cloud gaming for some of those; and how much space is free for games.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Steam can keep a game library on a USB drive or a second disk (Steam › Settings › Storage).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: game controllers work in Steam (Steam Input) and in Linux games: Xbox, PlayStation 4 and 5, Switch and Steam controllers, by USB and by Bluetooth. Keyboards and mice stay out of apps' reach.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Fixed: PlayStation 4 and 5 controllers ran as plain HID devices (no light bar, touchpad, motion or rumble): their driver was left out of the system without a word. It is now checked when Rudolf OS is built.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: Changed: notifications wait in the notification centre while a Linux app's window is full screen (a Steam game, Big Picture, a Windows game in Wine), as for full-screen pages.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Thunderbolt and USB4 docks, displays and devices that use PCIe over the cable (external drives and cards), and the Aquantia network chip of many docks. Where the computer protects its memory from devices on the cable (DMA protection), they are allowed by themselves; otherwise a new device asks once, an administrator allows it, and it is allowed by itself from then on. Settings › Devices lists them, with Forget.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: USB-C ports are managed by Rudolf OS (UCSI), and displays work through USB-C (DisplayPort alternate mode) where the port supports it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New (preview): the first part of built-in cameras on newer Intel laptops (Intel's camera processor IPU6 and IPU7, the camera's power and light, and the common sensors). Apps cannot use these cameras yet: that needs a later update. Until then Settings › Devices › Not supported yet lists the camera. USB cameras work as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.4 (2026-11-08)
docs.t: New: Settings › Security › Health log notes each package installed, updated or removed from the Rudolf OS Library, and each one refused (for example one signed by the Library that tries to bring a program).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: Summary: USB Wi-Fi adapters with Ralink and MediaTek RT2800 chips, a choice of Wi-Fi adapter, and a list of the devices that have no driver yet

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: New: USB Wi-Fi adapters with Ralink and MediaTek RT2800 chips work (RT2770, RT2870, RT3070, RT3071, RT3072, RT3370, RT3572, RT3573, RT5370, RT5372, RT5572: most inexpensive Wi-Fi dongles), and the same chips as cards inside older laptops (RT2860, RT3090, RT3290, RT5390 and others).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: New: Settings › Network › Wi-Fi: with a USB Wi-Fi adapter next to the built-in one, choose which one to use. Rudolf OS remembers it, uses it whenever it is plugged in, and goes back to the built-in Wi-Fi when it is unplugged.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: Fixed: the RT2800 driver was asked for but left out of the system without a word. Every Wi-Fi driver is now checked when Rudolf OS is built, so none can go missing again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: New: Settings › Devices › Not supported yet: the parts of this computer that Rudolf OS has no driver for yet, built in or plugged in (for example a Wi-Fi card, a sound processor, a camera or a fingerprint reader), or that every device has one. Report a problem includes the list, and the health log notes it the first time Rudolf OS starts on a computer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: New: Settings › Devices shows each USB device's speed and the port it is in ("USB 2.0, 480 Mbit/s, in a USB 3 port (10 Gbit/s)"). A USB device that does not say what it is (most Wi-Fi dongles) is named by what it calls itself.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: Fixed: Make a Rudolf OS USB stick could report a stick as ready that would not start ("this drive has boot files only"): made from an installed Rudolf OS, the stick needs that system copied onto it, and once it was not. The stick is now checked before it is called ready: its system must be complete and read back the same as this computer's, or it says what went wrong.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: Fixed: Install here from a Rudolf OS USB stick made by Make a Rudolf OS USB stick (or from an installed Rudolf OS) installed only the boot files, and the computer stopped at "this drive has boot files only". It now copies the running system too, and checks it before saying Rudolf OS is installed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.3 (2026-11-07)
docs.t: Fixed: Shut down, Restart and Sleep no longer cut off a job that would be left half done: making a USB stick, installing, writing boot files, setting up a drive for your files, a system update or encrypting your files. Rudolf OS says what it is still doing; "Restart anyway" (and the like) is there if you really mean it. A restart in the middle of Make a Rudolf OS USB stick had twice left a stick without its system.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: Summary: the Rudolf OS Library: Quake and Emu download when you first need them, and every update is smaller; Game Boy games in Emu's library; Windows games get the keyboard and full screen

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: New: App Store › Rudolf OS Library, a catalog of apps made for Rudolf OS that not every computer needs. Each shows its size, description and licence, with Get, Open, Update and Remove. The Library has its own signing key: it can add apps, but it can never change Rudolf OS itself.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: Changed: Quake's free game data and Emu's Nintendo DS player moved into the Library. They download (21 MB and 0.4 MB) the first time you ask for them, so every desktop update is about 12 MB smaller. SNES games play without a download, and Quake data you already have on drive C: stays.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: Changed: a computer that already played DS games gets Emu's DS player back by itself after the update, once.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: New: Emu's "Add games" takes Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance games (.gb, .gbc, .gba, or in a ZIP file). They go to Games › GB, show under Game Boy / GBA in Emu's library, and play in the Game Boy player.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: Fixed: a ZIP file whose game had a space in its name (most downloaded games) was skipped as "no SNES or DS game inside".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: Fixed: Windows games (Wine) got only some keys: the arrow keys worked, letters did not. A game in front now gets the keyboard the way Windows games expect (and gets it back when you click it after using the taskbar).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.2 (2026-11-06)
docs.t: Changed: a game that goes full screen now covers the whole screen, taskbar too, as Roblox does: whether it asks for full screen or makes its borderless window the size of the screen (as Windows games in Wine do, Starport GE among them). Switching the game to windowed brings the taskbar back. Super+Esc goes to the desktop, Super+Tab to the next window.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: Summary: Bluetooth (controllers, keyboards, mice, headphones), and Xbox Cloud Gaming and GeForce NOW in the Start menu

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: New: Bluetooth (Settings › Bluetooth), on computers with a Realtek Bluetooth chip or a USB Bluetooth adapter with one (Intel and MediaTek chips follow in an update). Pair controllers (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro), keyboards, mice and headphones: put the device in pairing mode, choose Search for devices, then Pair. No code to type. Paired devices reconnect by themselves; headphones become the sound output when they connect. Notifications say when a device connects, goes away, or its battery runs low.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: New: Xbox Cloud Gaming and GeForce NOW in the Start menu and the App Store's Games tab. They open in Oracle; controllers work in them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: New: game mode. While a game or video is full screen, notifications wait in the notification centre instead of popping up, and one message afterwards says how many came.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: Fixed: playing with only a controller did not count as using the computer, so the screen could lock or the computer sleep in the middle of a game.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: New: controllers are listed in Settings › Devices.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: Fixed: Bluetooth pairings were not kept: a device showed as paired, but after a restart it had to be paired again, and a phone asking to compare codes never got an answer. A phone's code now appears on screen to confirm (Yes / No), a device that asks to pair is asked about, a keyboard that needs a code shows it, and Settings says so when a pairing did not finish.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: Fixed: phones and other computers could not find this computer over Bluetooth. Settings › Bluetooth has Let this computer be found (for a few minutes), and Search for devices makes it visible too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.1 (2026-11-03)
docs.t: Fixed: Wi-Fi dropped every few minutes on laptops with a Realtek Wi-Fi chip (such as the RTL8821CE) when the router has both a 5 GHz and a 2.4 GHz radio. The chip's deep power saving is now off.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.0 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Summary: security: a firewall, encrypted data, administrators can open account files, a health log, and remote access from any browser

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.0 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: a firewall. Other computers can no longer connect to programs on this one (Linux and Windows programs included); everything this computer reaches out to works as before. Security Settings shows how many connections it blocked. The old "Firewall" setting for web pages is now called Website blocking; it works as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.0 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: Encrypt my data (Security Settings). Debian, Linux and Windows programs, Linux apps and files kept in Downloads move into a folder the system encrypts. Signing in with your password unlocks it; Guest does not. A recovery key, shown once, opens it if every password is forgotten.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.0 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: administrators can open the other accounts' files (in C:\USERS) and reset an account's password without its files being lost. It is on for every account and can be turned off per account (User Settings › Files and administrators). Each account's welcome file says who can open its files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.0 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: System health (Settings) records what happened on this computer: start-ups and how long they took, crashes, pages closed to free memory, updates that fell back, failed sign-ins, firewall blocks and remote sessions. It stays on this computer; Report a problem includes its latest events after you read the report.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.5.0 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: Remote access (Settings). Use this computer from a phone, tablet or another computer on the same network, in any web browser, with nothing to install. A pairing code is asked once per browser, then an account and its password. Someone at the computer allows each connection, unless an administrator lets that account connect unattended. A red bar shows who is connected, with End.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.9 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Summary: Windows programs in a click: install Wine from Settings, and installed programs appear in the Start menu

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.9 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: Install Wine from Settings › Apps › Linux, or straight from a Windows program that cannot open yet. No Terminal commands are needed: it downloads about 1 GB and says when it is done.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.9 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: Windows programs installed with Wine (games and their launchers) appear in the Start menu by themselves, with their own icons.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.9 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Fixed: programs that expect to start in their own folder (game launchers and updaters) are started there.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.9 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Fixed: Windows programs whose paths have backslashes (all of them) started with a wrong path from Wine's own menu entries.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.8 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Summary: Windows programs open with Wine, and Linux apps appear in the Start menu straight away

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.8 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: New: with Wine installed in Debian (Settings › Apps › Linux), Windows programs (.exe, .msi, .bat) open with it: double-click the file, or use Open with. Large downloads kept on the disk open the same way. Without Wine, opening a Windows program says how to get it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.8 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Fixed: a Linux app installed outside the Linux Terminal only appeared in the Start menu after signing in again or opening the Terminal. The Start menu now checks for new Linux apps each time it opens.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.8 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Fixed: Linux apps that only open files (such as Wine's program loader) were never offered in Open with.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.8 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Changed: the L in Rudolf now stands for Linux: Rudolf OS is the Runtime Driver Open Linux Framework (it was Lua). The sign-in screen, About Rudolf OS, VER and the Prompt say so, and so does C:\README.TXT, also on computers set up by an older version.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.8 (2026-11-02)
docs.t: Fixed: when a page filled the memory faster than Rudolf OS could move it to the compressed swap, the desktop could stall for up to half a minute before the page was closed. The page is now closed as soon as the system reports it is stalling with little memory left.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Summary: a page that uses up the memory no longer freezes the desktop: Rudolf OS closes that page and says why

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: compressed swap in memory. Rudolf OS keeps memory it is not using right now compressed in memory, so a computer holds about half as much again before it runs out (a 3.4 GB laptop holds about 5 GB). Task Manager shows how much is stored this way.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: when memory runs out anyway, Rudolf OS closes the web page using the most memory, and only that page. Oracle shows "This page was closed because it used too much memory" in its tab, with a Reload button, and a notification names the page. Before, the whole desktop could stop responding for a minute and then start again with every window and tab closed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Changed: if memory runs out, the desktop and what draws it are the last things the system closes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: Display Properties' Font list offered fonts Rudolf OS does not have. Tahoma, Verdana, Trebuchet MS, Georgia, Comic Sans MS and Lucida Console all looked the same. Every choice is now a real font, named with the font it stands in for ("Gelasio (like Georgia)"), and each one looks different. Three of them (Gelasio, Fira Sans, Comic Neue) are new in Rudolf OS. A font chosen in an older version keeps the look it had.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: Weather and its desktop widget showed Berlin until a city was searched for, and the widget never changed afterwards. They now show the city of your time zone (System Settings), or ask for your city when the time zone does not say. The widget follows the city chosen in Weather at once, and updates every 15 minutes; clicking it opens Weather.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: Weather shows °F and mph for places in the United States, with a °C/°F switch, and a city name with several matches (Springfield) lists them to choose from.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.7 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: with "Use it for games and the desktop" (Display Properties › Graphics), playing a large game in Oracle (Friday Night Funkin' on Newgrounds) could freeze a laptop with little memory and bring back the sign-in screen.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.6 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Summary: Notey in SpreadsheetPro and PresentPro as in WordPro, with help for each app; dark pages in Oracle, and its menu easier to read

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.6 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: Notey in SpreadsheetPro and PresentPro is the same Notey as in WordPro. He moves in held poses, a few frames a second (not a constant smooth bob), with his expressions, tricks and reactions. He can be dragged anywhere, and falls asleep when nothing happens. Hiding him in one app hides him in all three.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.6 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: in SpreadsheetPro, Notey checks a spreadsheet and fixes what he finds: - errors, explained, or shown as a blank instead; - numbers stored as text; - a formula unlike the ones around it; - a total that misses the last rows; - columns too narrow for their numbers; - long tables whose headings scroll away. He also explains the formula in any cell in words, finds the function you describe ("how do I work out an average?"), offers a total under a column of numbers or a chart for a table, and reminds you to save.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.6 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: in PresentPro, Notey checks a presentation: - slides without a title; - slides with too much text (he can split them in two); - text too small or too faint to read; - stretched pictures; - empty slides; - too many fonts; - missing speaker notes. He offers a theme and transitions as the deck grows, opens the themes, and rehearses the talk.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.6 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: dark pages in Oracle (☰ › Dark pages). Oracle's bar, tabs and menu turn dark, and so do the pages. Pages that are dark already are left as they are; pictures and videos keep their colours.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.6 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: Oracle's ☰ menu had light grey text on a white background when the desktop used the dark theme.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Summary: two new apps with WordPro: SpreadsheetPro, in the place of Excel, and PresentPro, in the place of PowerPoint; Shut down and Restart finish within seconds

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: SpreadsheetPro replaces the small Spreadsheet app. It has WordPro's menus and toolbar, 702 columns by 100,000 rows, several sheets, 167 functions (with a description as you type each one), number formats, fonts, colours, borders, merged cells, conditional formatting with colour scales and data bars, sorting, filters, data validation, find and replace, comments, named ranges, charts (column, bar, line, area, pie, doughnut and scatter) that follow the data, the fill handle for series, frozen panes, printing and PDF with page setup, and templates (a budget, an invoice, a timetable, a grade book, a loan calculator). It opens and saves Excel .xlsx files, CSV files, and the old Spreadsheet's files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: PresentPro replaces the Presentations app. Slides with eight layouts, twelve themes and a master (footer, date, slide numbers, logo); text, shapes, pictures (cropped, with a border and brightness), tables, charts and icons that can be moved, resized, rotated, aligned, grouped and layered, with guides that snap; speaker notes; sections and the slide sorter; transitions and animations. Presenting works with the keyboard and with a presenter remote, has a presenter view (P) with the notes, the next slide and the time, a pen and a laser pointer, black and white screens, rehearsed timings and a show that loops. It opens and saves PowerPoint .pptx files, makes PDFs of the slides, handouts and notes pages, pictures of the slides, and has templates (a talk, a lesson, a report, a photo album, a pitch). The old Presentations files open as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: the three apps work together. A range copied in SpreadsheetPro pastes as a table in WordPro and PresentPro, and a chart copies as a picture or with its data. WordPro's Insert menu has Spreadsheet table and Chart, and File › Send to PresentPro makes slides from a document's headings; PresentPro's File › Send to WordPro makes a handout. While there are unsaved changes, SpreadsheetPro and PresentPro keep a copy every minute and offer it after a crash or a power cut. The Start menu has an Office group with all three.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: Shut down and Restart could take half a minute, and stayed at "Please wait…" for good if a step of the desktop never finished. Every app is now asked to close at once and given 5 seconds at most, the desktop's own steps 3 seconds, and the data partition is made read-only before the power goes off. About › For developers shows how long the last shutdowns took. The power button set to Shut down now does so.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Changed: the desktop's right-click menu says "Open settings…" instead of "Change background…".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.5 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Removed: the Cyberdeck test in About › For developers.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Summary: the volume and brightness keys work; the clock sets itself from the internet; the taskbar shows the battery, the real network and one time; Power and battery settings; eight screen savers; a tidier Settings

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: the laptop's volume, mute, microphone and brightness keys work (on the ASUS Vivobook Go: F1 to F5), in the desktop, in games and in Linux apps alike, with an indicator showing the new level. The taskbar's volume is now the computer's own volume, which every app follows; a brightness icon sits next to it, and Settings › Volume Controls has System volume.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: System Settings › Power and battery: power mode (Power saver, Balanced, Performance), battery saver (on now, or by itself at 10, 20 or 30 %), turning the screen off and sleeping after a time without input, what closing the lid and pressing the power button do, and battery care (stop charging at 60 or 80 %), each for on battery and plugged in where it applies. The settings hold from the start, signed in or not.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: the battery on the taskbar, next to the workspace buttons, with its level, charging, and the time left or to full. A device's battery that reports -1 % is no longer listed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New: Display Properties › Screen saver: on or off, start after 1 to 60 minutes, eight styles (Starfield, Clock, Rudolf, Code rain, Mystify, Bubbles, Aurora, Fireworks) with a preview, the time over it, and the password when it ends. It is drawn by the processor, and it no longer starts while a game or a Linux app is being used.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: the clock could go back to 2016 after a restart (when the computer's own clock lost its time), and then no secure connection worked: no update check, no development link. Rudolf OS now never starts earlier than its release date, and sets the clock from the internet by itself at every start, when the network comes up and every 12 hours, keeping the result in the computer's clock.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: the calendar, the lock screen and the widgets showed another time than the taskbar (the browser's own time zone instead of the one set in System Settings). They all show the same time and date now.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: the network icon said "Ethernet — connected" on a laptop on Wi-Fi. It shows the real connection now: Wi-Fi with the network's name and signal, or the cable with its speed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed: the pointer speed in Mouse and touchpad was forgotten at every restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Changed: Settings is tidier. Mouse and touchpad has every pointer setting (one pointer speed, also for games); the language and the internet clock are in System Settings › Date, time and language; web search and downloads are on the Oracle page; Accessibility is grouped as Vision, Hearing and Voice control; the Cyberdeck test and updating the desktop page from a file are in About › For developers. Quick settings keeps its switches; volume, brightness and the battery have their own taskbar icons.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Removed: unused code and programs, and two Accessibility settings that did nothing (natural scrolling and horizontal scroll speed; natural scrolling is in Mouse and touchpad).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Changed (1.4.4 update): the taskbar has one network icon. Its menu now also shows the Wi-Fi networks in range and joins one, as the separate Wi-Fi icon did; that icon is gone.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: Fixed (1.4.4 update): on ASUS laptops F1 to F5 needed Fn for the volume and brightness (the keyboard started with Fn lock on). They now work on their own, as in Windows; Fn with them gives F1 to F5, and Fn+Esc switches.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.4 (2026-11-01)
docs.t: New (1.4.4 update): a picture of your own as the desktop background. Display Properties › Picture: choose one from your files or from this computer, and how it fills the screen (fill, fit, stretch, centre or tile). It is kept with your settings, so it stays after a restart even if the file is moved or deleted.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.3 (2026-10-30)
docs.t: Summary: games and apps that draw with OpenGL through X11, such as Oolite, start again

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.3 (2026-10-30)
docs.t: Fixed: apps and games that draw with OpenGL in an X11 window (Oolite among them, and many games made with SDL) stopped as soon as they started, because the display server offered no OpenGL to them ("GLX is not supported"). It now does, with the computer's own graphics driver.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.2 (2026-10-30)
docs.t: Summary: Google sign-in works in Oracle again; fixes 1.4.1 starting without its drivers (no Wi-Fi, slow screen) when an older Rudolf OS USB stick with its own files started the computer; the Rudolf OS boot entry works on more computers

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.2 (2026-10-30)
docs.t: Fixed: on a computer started through an older Rudolf OS USB stick that keeps its own files, the 1.4.1 update could start with the stick's older system instead of its own. Its drivers were then refused (each release signs its own), so there was no Wi-Fi and the screen was drawn without the graphics card, slowly. The update now starts only with its own system, from whichever drive holds it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.2 (2026-10-30)
docs.t: Fixed: Google refused to sign in from Oracle ("This browser or app may not be secure"), because Oracle's tabs said they were controlled by automation software. They no longer do.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.2 (2026-10-30)
docs.t: Fixed: on some computers (the ASUS Vivobook Go among them) the firmware skipped the "Rudolf OS" boot entry and started the drive through another entry, such as one made in its setup. Rudolf OS now takes the path of the entry that started it from the drive, so its own entry works on the next start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.1 (2026-10-28)
docs.t: Summary: a computer where Rudolf OS is installed starts from its own drive, without a USB stick (after Get new boot files, or a new Install here)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.1 (2026-10-28)
docs.t: Fixed: some computers (the ASUS Vivobook Go among them) could not start Rudolf OS from the drive it was installed on, only from a USB stick. Install here copied the disc image's partition table, which suits a stick but which a computer's firmware takes for an invalid table on an internal drive. Install here and Get new boot files (Settings › Security › Secure Boot) now give an internal drive a table the firmware accepts, a disk ID of its own, and a "Rudolf OS" entry first in the computer's boot order. An installed drive keeps its files; USB sticks are made as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.1 (2026-10-28)
docs.t: Fixed: the development link ran every earlier command again when it was switched on with another data partition (for example on a USB stick). Commands that already have a result are not run again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: Summary: the development link: let a developer you choose run tests on this computer through a private GitHub repository you own, while you watch and allow each command

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: New: Settings › Security › Development link. While it is on, a developer you choose (for example a Claude session) can run tests on this computer: run commands with full control, take screenshots, send files from it and bring files to it, and restart it. Commands and results go through a private GitHub repository you own; only people and sessions you give that repository to can use it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: It is off unless you switch it on, which asks for an administrator's password. It ends by itself after 1, 2, 4 or 8 hours, and stays on across a restart only if you tick that. A red banner across the top of the screen shows while it is on, with the time left and End now.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: Ask first (on unless you untick it): every command waits on the screen, with its full text, until you press Allow or Refuse.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: The GitHub token you paste is checked with GitHub (a private repository it can write to), kept where only the system can read it and never shown again; revoking it on GitHub ends all access. Files in home folders are not sent unless you allow it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: Settings shows a log of every command, its result and whether you allowed it (30 days). The system report says whether the link is on.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.4.0 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: Use it on a test computer only, never on one with personal files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.1 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: Summary: fixes 1.3.0 running an older Rudolf OS USB stick's system and files, instead of the computer's own, on computers started through such a stick

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.1 (2026-10-27)
docs.t: Fixed: on a computer where Rudolf OS is installed but which starts through an older Rudolf OS USB stick that keeps its own files (for example because the computer's firmware does not start its internal drive), the 1.3.0 update ran the stick's older system and files. The desktop then said, for example, "Rudolf OS 1.1", and Wi-Fi and settings were the stick's. The update now always runs from the drive that holds it, with that drive's files, whatever drive the computer started from. Nothing on either drive was changed or erased.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Summary: App Store › Games lists every game on Flathub, with search and genres; a USB stick uses its own files on a computer where Rudolf OS is installed; crashes are reported as crashes; the Linux password can be changed

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: a Rudolf OS USB stick started on a computer where Rudolf OS is installed could run from the computer's own drive instead, with its files (on a laptop with an NVMe drive it usually did, because that drive is ready first). Rudolf OS now starts from the kind of drive the computer's firmware started (a USB stick or an internal drive), and uses that drive's files when it has its own; otherwise it works as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: when a part of Rudolf OS crashes during a task (as the app list reader did in 1.2.8), the task says so, with Report a problem, instead of guessing ("Is this computer connected to the internet?"). The system report lists such crashes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Settings › Apps › Linux › Change the Linux password… sets a new password for Debian (the one sudo asks for). Before, it could only be chosen when Debian was set up.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Changed: updates rebuild every Rudolf OS program, so fixes to the package tool, the assistant and printing reach installed computers too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: App Store › Games lists every game in Flathub's app list under "All games on Flathub", with a search box, genres (action, arcade, board, emulators, puzzles, role-playing, simulation, sports, strategy and more) and "Verified only". Installed games come first.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: Linux apps › Games left out games that list only their genre (for example "Action") and not "Game".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.3.0 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: Command Prompt said "Rudolf OS [Version 1.1]" (when it opens and for VER), and Lua's sys.version() said "Rudolf OS 1.0", whatever the version. Both now give the version that is installed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.9 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Summary: the App Store's Linux app list downloads again; signing in to Roblox in Sober (and web pages inside other Linux apps) works

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.9 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: Sober could not sign in to Roblox: its sign-in window stayed blank with "No such interface org.freedesktop.portal.ProxyResolver", then "Something went wrong". Linux apps from the App Store ask Rudolf OS which proxy to use for each address; Rudolf OS now answers (its own proxy from Settings › Network, or none), and says whether the computer is online.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.9 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: App Store › Linux apps › Download the app list stopped with "Segmentation fault" and "Is this computer connected to the internet?". Flathub's catalogue has empty entries (such as an empty paragraph), and the program that reads it crashed on them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.9 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: release updates now rebuild the desktop portal and the app catalogue reader for Linux apps too (before, only a full build did).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Summary: the Linux terminal and App Store apps work on computers running an installed update; new boot files for an installed computer without erasing it (Secure Boot on computers installed from an older disc); webcams work, with a camera switch in Settings › Privacy; the hardware check tests the keyboard, touchpad, camera, battery and screen

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: the Linux terminal (Debian) could not be set up or started, with "the Debian sandbox did not start: mounting /proc failed (Operation not permitted)", on every computer running an installed update (since 1.2.3). The start-up options were mounted over /proc/cmdline there, and the kernel then refuses a sandbox its own /proc. Flatpak apps from the App Store were refused the same way. Settings › Apps › Linux › Check now tests this too ("A new /proc for sandboxes").

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Settings › Security › Secure Boot › Get new boot files: a computer installed from a disc older than 1.2.2 can start with Secure Boot on without being reinstalled. Download the boot image (rudolf-os-X.Y.Z-boot.iso and its .sha256) from the Rudolf OS releases; Rudolf OS checks it, keeps a copy, and writes it at the next start in front of your files, which stay as they are. The installed system then starts from the installed update.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Install here › Replace the boot files only: the same for another drive Rudolf OS is installed on, from a USB stick, for example to repair one whose boot files were damaged.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: the disc releases have a boot image (rudolf-os-X.Y.Z-boot.iso, about 27 MB) next to the disc image.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: webcams work (USB Video Class, built-in laptop cameras included), in the Camera app, in websites (which still ask first) and in Linux apps.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Settings › Privacy › Camera: one switch that turns the camera off for everything; its driver is not loaded until it is switched on again, also after a restart.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: the hardware check (Task Manager › Hardware) has five more steps: every key of the keyboard (as laid out in the chosen layout), the touchpad or mouse (moving, both buttons, scrolling), the camera, the battery's health (its capacity compared with new, and its charge cycles) and the screen (one colour at a time, to spot dead pixels).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.8 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Changed: a factory reset of a drive that has boot files only keeps its installed system (everything else is erased as before).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Summary: a disc image downloaded in parts can be made into a USB stick without joining it by hand; making a stick over an older Rudolf OS stick works again; a check for Linux apps and the terminal; more USB Wi-Fi adapters work; a power button on the login screen; Luau and Pilot.lua checks are ready straight away; Files copies whole folders from a USB drive

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Make a USB stick and Install here accept a Rudolf OS disc image downloaded from GitHub in parts (rudolf-os-X.Y.Z.iso.part00, part01, ...). The parts are joined in order, checked against the .sha256 downloaded with them, and then written; a missing, short or damaged part is named and nothing is written. The joined image stays in Downloads.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: Make a USB stick refused to erase a stick that held an older Rudolf OS ("a file on it is still open"). (1.2.6)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: Install here and Make a USB stick with a downloaded disc image stopped at once without a message, and wrote nothing. (1.2.4)

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Changed: downloads are in one place, C:\DOWNLOADS, which Files' "Downloads" now opens. Large files are kept on the disk and shown there.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Changed: the disc files of a Rudolf OS release (the .iso, its parts and .sha256) downloaded from the Rudolf OS releases on GitHub are no longer blocked as unknown or program files. The same names from anywhere else still are.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Settings › Security › Secure Boot, Make a USB stick and Install here say when this Rudolf OS started from boot files older than Secure Boot support (a disc before 1.2.2), and how to get newer ones: make a stick from a newer disc image.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Settings › Apps › Linux › Check: what Linux apps and the terminal need from this computer (the data partition, temporary files, user namespaces, Flatpak's folders, the Debian sandbox), with what is wrong. It is also in the system report. When the Debian sandbox does not start, it now says which step failed and why.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Fixed: Flatpak apps could not be installed ("open(O_TMPFILE): No such file or directory") when Flatpak's repository had lost its tmp folder; it is made again at start-up. /var/tmp is made at start-up too.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: more USB Wi-Fi adapters work: Atheros AR9271 and AR7010 (TP-Link TL-WN722N v1 and many others), MediaTek MT7601U, MT7610U and MT7612U (among them Alfa AWUS036ACM). Plug one in and it appears in Settings › Network.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: Changed: Blitzen and Code Editor get the Luau type checker ready in the background as soon as Luau or Pilot.lua is chosen, or a .LUAU file is opened, so the first check no longer waits for it to load (up to two minutes on a slower computer). Switching between Luau, Roblox and Pilot.lua scripts no longer loads it again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: the login screen has a power button (bottom right) to shut down, restart or put the computer to sleep without signing in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.7 (2026-10-26)
docs.t: New: Files › a USB drive or memory card › Copy into Rudolf OS copies whole folders, with everything in them, into Downloads. It shows how far it has got and can be cancelled; files over 256 MB and files that cannot be read are left out and listed; a folder that does not fit is refused before anything is copied.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.6 (2026-10-25)
docs.t: Summary: Check this disc no longer reports a good disc as damaged; Make a Rudolf OS USB stick works with a stick that is already formatted

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.6 (2026-10-25)
docs.t: Fixed: "Check this disc or USB drive for errors" (in the start menu) said every disc and stick was damaged, because of one file (boot/rboot.bin) that is changed while the disc image is written. A 1.2.6 disc or stick passes. The result now says how many files were checked and names the damaged ones (Settings › Update and recovery shows the last result).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.6 (2026-10-25)
docs.t: Fixed: on a computer with an update installed, the check ran twice (once before the update started, once after) and the first result was lost. It now runs once. A disc or stick made before 1.2.6 still runs its own check first and shows the false error there; the second check, from this update, gives the right answer and is the one Settings shows.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.6 (2026-10-25)
docs.t: Fixed: Make a Rudolf OS USB stick and Install here refused a USB stick that Rudolf OS had opened by itself when it was plugged in (any stick formatted in the shop), with "is in use. Unmount its partitions first". Rudolf OS now closes the drive itself, and nothing on it is opened again while it is written. If a file on it is still open, the message says to close File Explorer or the app using it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.6 (2026-10-25)
docs.t: Changed: the erase question before making a stick names what is on the drive now (its name and format).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: Summary: make a Rudolf OS USB stick from Rudolf OS; check this computer's hardware; apps over Wi-Fi; a Games page; Restart into Windows; Blitzen writes Luau and Pilot.lua

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Blitzen has three more languages. Lua is plain Lua 5.3, without the BlockLua rules. Luau is Roblox's Lua (types, continue, +=, string interpolation): Blitzen checks the types with Luau's own checker, then runs the program on this computer. Roblox game scripts are checked but not run, since they need Roblox. Pilot.lua is for Waste of Space microcontrollers: every part call is checked against Pilot.lua's definitions, then the program runs with stand-in parts that say what they were asked to do.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: when Luau code has a type error, Blitzen sees the error and its line and fixes the program, as it already did for programs that fail when run.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Code Editor opens .LUAU files and runs them (Luau and Pilot.lua), and "Ask Blitzen" picks Luau or Pilot.lua for them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Linux apps and Roblox (Sober) install over Wi-Fi, not only over a network cable. Before a download of more than 500 MB over Wi-Fi the App Store says how much it is and how much space is free, and asks.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Settings › Network › Saved networks: mark a network Metered (a phone hotspot, a capped plan) and the App Store asks before any download over 50 MB on it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: an app download that stops (the Wi-Fi drops, the router restarts) is tried again by itself, and Get continues where it stopped instead of starting over.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
