docs.t: New: App Store › Games: Roblox, Steam, Minecraft (Prism Launcher), RetroArch and the games built into Rudolf OS, each with its download size and whether it needs the graphics card. When Rudolf OS draws with the processor, the page says which games will be slow and why.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Settings › Storage and backup › Make a Rudolf OS USB stick: puts this Rudolf OS (with its installed updates), or a downloaded image, on a USB stick or memory card of 2 GB or more. The copy is read back and checked, the stick keeps files from its first start, and it can take your files and settings with it. No Windows, Rufus or joining of parts is needed any more.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Back up to a USB stick (Settings › Storage and backup): the backup is written straight to a plugged-in drive, with a checksum, and read back. On a new Rudolf OS, the first-start screen has Restore from a backup on a USB stick, which finds it there and refuses a damaged one.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: Changed: Install here reads the copy back and compares it before it finishes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Task Manager › Hardware › Check this computer…: a guided check of about a minute: sound (a tone: did you hear it?), microphone (a level meter), network (wired speed with the cable hint, Wi-Fi networks in range, a download from the update server), USB (plug in a stick), graphics (what draws the screen, frames per second) and, if you like, sleep for 10 seconds. The results go into the system report, so a problem report shows them (nothing personal is in it).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: Fixed: joining a Wi-Fi network for the first time after starting could fail with "out of range, or the password is wrong" on slower computers, because Rudolf OS gave up after 20 seconds while it was still scanning. It now waits up to a minute.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Restart into Windows (in the Power dialog and in Settings › Update and recovery) on a computer that also has Windows: the computer starts Windows Boot Manager once, then comes back to the Rudolf OS menu as before. It works with Secure Boot on.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: New: Settings › Update and recovery › Boot menu: choose what the UEFI boot menu starts when nobody chooses (for example Start from memory) and how long it waits. The choice is kept in the computer's firmware, so the disc or stick is not changed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.5 (2026-10-23)
docs.t: Updated: Chromium 156 and Linux 6.18.58 (security fixes).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Summary: a USB stick written from the image can keep your files; Secure Boot key enrolment works on more computers; clearer graphics and network status

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: a USB stick written with Rufus or Etcher can keep your files, settings and apps. After you sign in, Rudolf OS offers to use the stick's free space (Settings › Storage and backup › Keep files on this drive); restart once and everything you made so far moves onto it. App Store apps such as Roblox (Sober) need this.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Fixed: on some computers (ASUS among them) the blue Secure Boot screen refused rudolf.cer with "Unsupported Format". The boot files now carry their lowercase names. On older discs, Settings › Security Settings › Prepare Secure Boot always works.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: "Install here…" can install a newer disc image you downloaded (Install from), so an older stick can install a Secure Boot ready system. Only images signed by Rudolf OS are accepted.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: Task Manager › System and the system report say what draws the screen (the graphics card and its name, or the processor), what web pages are drawn with, and the NVIDIA GSP firmware state.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: a wired network running slower than its chip (100 Mb/s on gigabit Ethernet) is pointed out, with a hint about the cable or router port.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: AMD processors get AMD's latest microcode at every start (security fixes such as SRSO), without a BIOS update.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: the disc download has join.ps1 for Windows: it joins the parts, checks them and names a missing or damaged part. JOIN-PARTS.TXT has PowerShell commands, and warns never to keep the image on the stick being written.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Changed: Settings › Update and recovery says when an update has been kept after a successful start.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.4 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Changed: the README covers the UEFI boot menu, keeping files, installing from a downloaded image and what to do when Windows says the stick is not accessible.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Summary: graphics acceleration for NVIDIA GeForce 20, 30 and 40 series cards, and fixes found on a real computer

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20, 30 and 40 series (and GTX 16) cards draw with the graphics card instead of the processor. Rudolf OS now carries NVIDIA's GSP firmware and Mesa's NVK driver, which these cards need for any acceleration with the open driver. The first start after the update can take a few seconds longer while the card starts its firmware. If the card cannot use it, Rudolf OS draws with the processor as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: New: the firmware for Realtek Ethernet chips (the r8169 driver) is included.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Fixed: Task Manager › System › Installed release and the system report now show the release that is running (version, serial, channel, slot).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Fixed: Task Manager says "USB drive" or "SD card" when Rudolf OS started from one; it said "disc" for a disc image written to a USB stick.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Fixed: saving a window as PDF no longer turns dashes, quotes and table columns into "?".

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Fixed: the start-up options in Task Manager and the system report no longer list the same options twice.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.3 (2026-10-19)
docs.t: Note: the update is larger than usual (about 75 MB) because of the NVIDIA firmware.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Summary: Rudolf OS starts with Secure Boot on: enroll its key once, and the computer starts only signed, checked software

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Secure Boot. UEFI computers no longer need Secure Boot turned off. The first time, a blue screen asks to enroll the Rudolf OS key (Enroll key from disk › EFI › rudolf › rudolf.cer); after that Rudolf OS starts as before. Already running Rudolf OS? Settings › Security Settings › Prepare Secure Boot does it with a one-time password, then turn Secure Boot on in the firmware settings.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: UEFI computers have a boot menu: Start, Recovery mode, Check this disc or USB drive, Start from memory, and Debug start (only with Secure Boot off).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Security: every system file is checked as it is read (dm-verity) against the signed release list, with Secure Boot on or off; a damaged or changed layer is caught.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Security: with Secure Boot on, the kernel is locked down: only signed drivers and signed updated kernels start, and nothing can write to kernel memory. An update whose files fail the check is dropped and the previous system starts.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Task Manager › System and the system report show whether Secure Boot is on, the lockdown and whether the system layers were checked.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.2 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Note: to use Secure Boot, write the 1.2.2 disc image to the USB stick or disc; an older stick keeps working with Secure Boot off. Computers that started in BIOS (legacy) mode are not affected.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Summary: download files of any size from websites, up to 4 GB by default; large files stay on the disk and open from C:\DOWNLOADS

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: downloads are no longer limited to 1.5 MB. Files up to 1.5 MB go into C:\DOWNLOADS as before; larger ones are kept on the disk (in the Downloads folder that Linux apps see) and C:\DOWNLOADS shows them with 💽 and their real size.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: videos, music, pictures and PDFs kept on the disk open in Rudolf OS and are read in pieces, so a large video starts at once. Text files up to 4 MB open read-only. Other kinds of large files can be opened in Linux apps.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Settings > Network > Downloads > Largest download (100 MB to 16 GB, 4 GB at first). about:downloads shows the progress of a download and what was checked.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Settings > Storage lists the downloads kept on the disk and how much space is free. Rudolf OS warns when the disk is over 90% full; running live, downloads are kept in memory until you shut down.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: PDF, ZIP and other archives, more video and audio formats, fonts and subtitles are recognized file types.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Security: every download still goes through the file-type rules and the antivirus. For files over 8 MB the antivirus checks the first and last 4 MB, and about:downloads says so. Program files wait in a quarantine folder until an administrator approves them. Files kept on the disk are never run as pages of the desktop.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Changed: renaming or deleting a large download in C:\DOWNLOADS does the same on the disk (deleting it keeps it in the Trash until the Trash is emptied). Large downloads cannot be copied elsewhere in C: (files up to 1.5 MB can). Backups contain a note of them, not the files.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.1 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Changed: Chromium's own Safe Browsing check of downloads is off; it needed a connection to Google and held downloads in place. Rudolf OS's antivirus checks them.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Summary: Oracle's tabs are real browser tabs, so signing in to websites works inside Oracle; a new Task Manager shows the kernel, the services and the hardware; report a problem with the computer's status in one step

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Oracle opens websites as real browser tabs. Signing in works inside Oracle for every site (Google, Microsoft, banks…), pop-up sign-ins keep working, and each Rudolf OS account has its own cookies. The browser window for sign-in sites is no longer needed.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Rudolf OS moves to its new desktop host by itself once, shortly after starting (a few seconds; your files, ROMs, game saves and settings move along). If it cannot start, the desktop runs as before. Settings > Oracle sign-in > Real browser tabs turns it off.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: downloads from websites go to C:\DOWNLOADS through the firewall, file-type and antivirus checks, also files that need you to be signed in.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: a website or a video can go fullscreen; Esc brings it back. Games can capture the mouse pointer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Fixed: Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+N could close or quit the desktop or open a browser window over it. Ctrl+W now closes an Oracle tab, Ctrl+T opens one, and Ctrl+Q does nothing harmful. Linux apps get these keys unchanged.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Task Manager: Processes (every process grouped by what it is, with CPU and memory, and End process), Performance (CPU, memory and network), System (Rudolf OS, the desktop's host, the services with Restart, the kernel, its drivers and warnings), Hardware (processor, graphics, display, storage, network adapters, sound, input devices, battery). Apps lists Oracle's real tabs with the memory each page uses.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: New: Report a problem (Task Manager, or Start): opens a ready-filled report on the Rudolf OS issue tracker on GitHub, with the state of the computer at that moment. It leaves out your name, files, web and network addresses and Wi-Fi names; you review it before sending, or save it to send later.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Security: ending a system process or restarting a service asks for an administrator's password; the processes Rudolf OS needs cannot be ended. Websites in Oracle keep their own protection against being shown inside other pages.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Fixed: with the newer Chromium that security updates bring, Rudolf OS's browser settings were not applied, so the system's own file dialog (which froze some PCs) could open again, and real tabs could not start. Both work again.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.2.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.t: Known limits: a few websites forbid the script that makes fullscreen work and stay in their window; downloads are limited to 1.5 MB as before.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Summary: signing in to websites works (Oracle moves sign-in pages to a real browser window); choose the screen resolution and frame rate; fixes for small screens and display scaling

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Fixed: signing in to websites in Oracle did not last: the site accepted the password, then asked again. Oracle shows websites inside the desktop, where Chromium drops their sign-in cookies. Sites that need a sign-in now move to a real browser window (🌐 in the taskbar switches between it and the desktop).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Oracle notices when a page asks for a password and offers to open it in the browser window, or does it by itself when you send a sign-in or press "Sign in with Google / Microsoft / Apple…". Nothing you type is read.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Settings > Oracle sign-in: your sign-in sites, and whether Oracle asks first. Google, Microsoft, Yahoo, banks and payment sites always open in the browser window.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Security: sign-in sites, banks and payment sites keep their own protection against being shown inside other pages.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Flash content plays in the browser window too (Ruffle).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Settings > Display > Resolution: Automatic, 1920×1080, 1366×768, 1280×720 or 1024×576. On a screen of another shape the picture keeps its shape, with black bars, and is scaled smoothly; touchscreens still touch the right spot.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Settings > Display > Frame rate: 120, 90, 60 or 30 fps. 90 and 120 need a monitor that offers them and the graphics-card display; 30 saves power.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: after changing the resolution or frame rate, "Keep this display setting?" — the previous setting comes back by itself after 15 seconds, or after 90 seconds if the screen shows nothing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.2 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Fixed: with display scaling above 100%, the Start menu ran off the top of the screen, and windows, the Calculator and the file picker could be larger than small screens such as 1024×576.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Summary: choosing files no longer freezes some PCs; laptop touchpads work; plugged-in devices are recognised and USB drives open in File Explorer

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Fixed: choosing a file (Files > Upload, Open a file, From computer, Import) froze the whole screen on some PCs, so the computer had to be switched off. Rudolf OS now uses its own file picker, which lists Downloads, Documents, Pictures and every drive.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Fixed: the touchpads of most laptops did not work, because drivers they need were missing (Intel LPSS, the Intel and AMD GPIO controllers, ELAN, Synaptics and Elantech).

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: touchpad gestures: tap to click (two fingers for a right click, three for a middle click), two-finger scrolling up, down and sideways, and a right click in a clickpad's bottom-right corner. Taps are ignored while you type.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Settings > Mouse and touchpad: pointer speed, acceleration, tap to click, natural scrolling and ignoring the touchpad while typing.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: plugged-in devices are recognised. A notification names each USB device (keyboard, mouse, game controller, camera, audio device, printer, Wi-Fi adapter and more) and says when Rudolf OS has no driver for it.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: USB drives and SD cards open by themselves in File Explorer's Drives list; the notification opens them. ⏏ Eject makes a drive safe to unplug.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: Settings > Devices lists the connected drives, USB devices, keyboards, mice and touchpads.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: New: after an update, a notification tells you what changed, and "What's new" shows every version's changes.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Fixed: game controllers no longer move the mouse pointer.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1.1 (2026-10-13)
docs.t: Security: drives are mounted without device files, set-user-ID or programs run from them, and websites cannot open the system's file dialog.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: Boots on real computers: Rudolf Boot (BIOS) and UEFI, from DVD or USB; install to disk with saved data; recovery mode, updates with rollback, factory reset.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: Task Manager, App Store with sandboxed apps, Code Editor, Image and PDF viewers, Screenshot and screen recording, Calendar, Clock, Spreadsheet, Presentations, Contacts, Weather, Characters & Emoji, Event Viewer, Camera, Voice Recorder, Font Viewer, Developer Console.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: Alt+Tab, workspaces, overview, Start search, notification centre, quick settings, calendar flyout, pinned and grouped taskbar buttons, desktop files and widgets, resize from any edge.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: New File Explorer with tabs, split view, preview, thumbnails, search inside files, undo, ZIP, Open with and drives.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: Encrypted home folders, stronger passwords, lock screen, administrator prompts, guest account and parental controls, backups.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: Screen reader, magnifier, dark and high-contrast themes, scaling, keyboard and mouse assistance, input methods, Arabic and Hebrew.

docs.h: Rudolf OS changes › 1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.t: Emu (Super Nintendo and Nintendo DS), Blitzen (offline coding assistant), Linux apps from Flathub and a Debian 13 terminal.
